request: We should know which of our contacts are most influential so we can prioritize them.
executive_summary: This release will introduce a feature to categorize government contacts by their level of influence, allowing users to prioritize interactions accordingly. However, the implementation details regarding the ongoing maintenance and review of influence assessments remain under discussion. The organization still needs to clarify specific regulations on data handling and review criteria for influence levels.

core_commitments.text: Users can view the influence level of each contact in the Government CRM.
core_commitments.note: Users will be able to view the influence level of each contact in the Government CRM, providing a clear understanding of their relationships.

core_commitments.text: Users are able to sort and filter contacts based on their influence level.
core_commitments.note: Users are able to sort and filter contacts based on their influence level, ensuring that prioritization can easily occur.

in_scope.text: A new field called 'Influence Level' will be added to each contact record in the Government CRM.
in_scope.note: A new field called 'Influence Level' will be added to each contact record to facilitate the categorization process.

in_scope.text: Influence Level will be categorized into three levels: 'High', 'Medium', and 'Low'.
in_scope.note: The influence level will be categorized into three levels: 'High', 'Medium', and 'Low', providing a simple and understandable classification.

in_scope.text: Users will be able to filter the contacts list to show only those with 'High' influence.
in_scope.note: Users will be able to filter the contacts list to show only those with 'High' influence, making it easier to focus on key contacts.

in_scope.text: Training materials will be developed and must include clear guidelines, practical examples, and assessments that require users to demonstrate their understanding and application of the influence categorization process.
in_scope.note: Training materials will include guidelines, practical examples, and assessments to ensure users effectively understand the influence categorization process.

in_scope.text: Users can view the influence status directly on the contact detail pages.
in_scope.note: Users can view the influence status directly on contact detail pages, facilitating quick access to essential classification information.

in_scope.text: Only designated team members, such as regional coordinators and project managers, will have the authority to assign and alter the 'Influence Level' for contacts.
in_scope.note: Only designated team members will have the authority to assign and alter 'Influence Level', ensuring that only qualified individuals handle this sensitive data.

out_of_scope.text: This release will not include automatic determination of influence levels; these will be manually assigned by designated team members.
out_of_scope.note: Automatic determination of influence levels will not be included to maintain a high level of accuracy through manual assessments.

out_of_scope.text: This release will not add any predictive analytics or algorithms to determine future influence.
out_of_scope.note: This release will not include predictive analytics or algorithms as the focus is on current influence levels only.

out_of_scope.text: The feature will not include influence tracking over time; it will focus solely on current influence levels.
out_of_scope.note: Influence tracking over time will not be incorporated as the feature will focus solely on current levels, streamlining implementation.

assumptions.text: It is assumed that designated team members will have the authority to classify influence levels, based on their knowledge of contacts.
assumptions.note: It is assumed that designated team members will classify influence levels based on their knowledge, ensuring informed decisions.

assumptions.text: It is assumed that users will have adequate training to understand how to use the new influence categorization feature.
assumptions.note: Adequate training is assumed to be in place for users to effectively engage with the influence categorization feature.

assumptions.text: It is assumed that there are existing procedures for updating contact information, which will include the new influence level field.
assumptions.note: Existing procedures for updating contact information will include the new influence level field, but ownership for these processes needs clarification.

assumptions.text: It is assumed that existing security and privacy regulations on sensitive data handling will be adhered to in the feature deployment.
assumptions.note: Existing security and privacy regulations will be adhered to during the deployment, but specifics on which regulations apply still need defining.

definitions.text: 'Influence Level' means a classification assigned to a contact based on their ability to affect decisions or outcomes related to the organization's activities.
definitions.note: 'Influence Level' is clearly defined as a classification that reflects a contact's ability to affect organizational outcomes, enhancing clarity.

definitions.text: 'High', 'Medium', 'Low' influence means the following: 'High' indicates significant decision-making power or authority, 'Medium' indicates moderate influence without decision-making power, and 'Low' indicates minimal influence on decision-making.
definitions.note: The definitions of 'High', 'Medium', and 'Low' are clear and outlined, aiding users in consistent assessment.

definitions.text: The criteria for assigning 'Influence Level' will be based on the contact's role, previous engagement history, and demonstrated ability to influence decisions related to the organization's activities.
definitions.note: Criteria for assigning influence levels are now defined, providing a consistent framework that mitigates subjectivity in evaluations.

success_criteria.text: At least 75% of users report that the influence categorization has improved their prioritization of contacts, measured through user feedback surveys.
success_criteria.note: User feedback surveys will measure the success criterion, focusing on whether the influence categorization improves prioritization.

open_questions.question: What process is in place to ensure that influence levels are regularly reviewed and updated?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Regular updates are critical to maintain the accuracy and relevance of influence assessments as relationships evolve.
options: Assign specific individuals for periodic evaluations
Outline a process for user feedback on influence levels

proposer.text: The process for regularly reviewing and updating influence levels must be determined by the organization to ensure data accuracy and responsiveness to changing relationships.

critic.text: The proposal needs a specific process for regularly updating influence levels, which requires organizational input.

open_questions.question: What specific criteria will define 'High', 'Medium', and 'Low' influence, and who will be responsible for establishing them?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Clearly defined criteria are essential for consistent and objective influence level assignments, reducing bias.
options: Create a committee to define criteria
Use existing data relationships as a guide

proposer.text: The establishment of specific criteria for 'High', 'Medium', and 'Low' influence and the appointment of responsible parties must be defined by the organization to avoid subjective bias.

critic.text: Criteria for 'High', 'Medium', and 'Low' influence assignments must be specified by the organization.

open_questions.question: Who is explicitly responsible for maintaining and updating the influence levels in contacts?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Clarifying ownership prevents data inaccuracies that could arise following personnel changes.
options: Assign a specific role to manage updates
Establish a collaborative process for updating influenced levels
Define a fallback process for absent team members

proposer.text: Explicit ownership for maintaining and updating the influence levels must be assigned by the organization to prevent outdated data following personnel changes.

critic.text: There needs to be clear ownership defined for updating and maintaining influence levels.

open_questions.question: Which specific security and privacy regulations will govern the handling of influence level data?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Clarity on applicable regulations is essential for ensuring compliance and protecting sensitive information throughout the categorization process.
options: Consult legal for detailed compliance requirements
Review existing GDPR and data protection guidelines

proposer.text: Specific security and privacy regulations impacting the handling of influence level data need to be clarified by the organization to ensure compliance.

critic.text: The applicable regulations regarding data handling are not specified and need human decision.

open_questions.question: What measures will be put in place to ensure that users are adequately trained to understand and apply influence classifications?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Effective training is crucial to ensure accurate use of the influence categorization feature and improve engagement efforts with contacts.
options: Follow-up training sessions to reinforce knowledge

proposer.text: The revised training requirement ensures that users must actively demonstrate their understanding of the influence levels, enhancing the effectiveness of the training materials.

critic.text: While the proposal commits to assessments in the training materials, it remains unclear how effective these measures will be in truly ensuring user understanding and application of influence classifications.

open_questions.question: What is the procedure if a designated team member responsible for assigning influence levels is unavailable?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A fallback process is essential to maintain workflow and responsiveness to urgent needs despite personnel absences.
options: Develop alternative access for influence assignment

proposer.text: The organization must define a fallback process for when designated team members are unavailable to assign or update influence levels.

critic.text: A clear fallback process needs to be defined for absent team members who assign influence levels.

tension.summary: The primary tension revolved around the necessity for a clear and consistent process for maintaining and updating influence assessments, as well as the definitions guiding influence categorization. While both parties acknowledged the importance of these processes, the proposer favored a flexible approach, while the critic insisted on specific guidelines, leaving several key questions open for further resolution.

proposer.worry: There may still be ambiguity in how influence levels are maintained and updated over time.

critic.worry: Inaccurate influence assessments could still arise from subjective evaluations despite clearer criteria.
